common_name: White Wonder Caladium (Classic Chartreuse-White Fancy-Leaf Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost when soil has warmed to at least 65°F; plant 1-2 inches deep in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in shade to partial shade.

directions: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in shade to partial shade. White Wonder is a classic fancy-leaf caladium bearing large, heart-shaped leaves in a pale chartreuse-white with prominent dark green veining and margin, a heavily traditional white-and-green pattern that has kept it in commercial and home-garden circulation for generations. Unlike sun-tolerant strap-leaf types bred more recently, White Wonder performs best in fuller shade, where its thin-textured fancy leaves resist the scorching that direct sun can cause. Mass planted beneath trees or along a shaded foundation, its pale coloring brightens dark corners effectively. Lift tubers before the first fall frost in climates outside its hardiness range and store dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

common_name: June Bride Caladium (Classic Ruffled White Strap-Leaf Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost when soil has warmed to at least 65°F; plant 1-2 inches deep in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade. June Bride bears crisp white, gently ruffled leaves with fine green veining, a clean and simple bridal-white color that has kept it a long-standing favorite for pairing with pink- or red-leaved caladium cultivars in a mixed bed. Its ruffled leaf margin adds subtle texture without the bold speckling or heavy variegation found in more elaborate fancy-leaf cultivars. Mass planted beneath trees or along a shaded walkway, it brightens dim corners of the garden effectively. Lift tubers before the first fall frost in climates outside its hardiness range and store dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

common_name: Mrs. Arno Nehrling Caladium (Classic Pink-and-Green Fancy-Leaf Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost when soil has warmed to at least 65°F; plant 1-2 inches deep in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade; named for the wife of noted Florida horticulturist Arno Nehrling.

directions: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade. Mrs. Arno Nehrling bears heart-shaped leaves in soft rose-pink with darker pink veining set against a green margin, a classic Florida-bred fancy-leaf caladium named for the wife of Arno Nehrling, a horticulturist influential in the early development of the Florida caladium industry. Its softer, blended pink tone works well massed as a large-scale groundcover or mixed with white- and red-leaved cultivars for a layered color display in a shaded bed. Lift tubers before the first fall frost in climates outside its hardiness range and store dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

Kathleen bears rosy-pink, heart-shaped leaves with a deeper pink center and green margin on a more compact plant than many fancy-leaf caladiums, making it a practical choice for smaller shaded beds, borders, and container plantings where taller caladium cultivars would crowd out neighboring plants. Its manageable size and reliable pink coloring make it a dependable filler for mixed shade containers alongside ferns or begonias. planting.note: Plant tubers in spring after the last frost when soil has warmed to at least 65°F; plant 1-2 inches deep in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade.

Marie Moir bears narrow, lance-shaped leaves splashed with pink and cream over a green background, an older heirloom strap-leaf caladium whose narrower, more pointed leaf shape and mottled pattern distinguish it from the broader, solid-colored strap-leaf cultivars bred more recently. Its compact size and mottled, informal color pattern suit a naturalistic shade bed or mixed container planting. Lift tubers before the first fall frost in climates outside its hardiness range and store dry over winter for replanting the following spring.

Pink Cloud bears large heart-shaped leaves in a soft, pale pink washed with a slightly deeper rose along the veins, a gentle, blended color that reads as a soft haze rather than the sharply contrasting patterns of many fancy-leaf caladiums, giving the plant its cloud-like namesake. It combines well with darker pink or red caladium cultivars for a layered pink color scheme in a large shaded bed. Lift tubers before the first fall frost in climates outside its hardiness range and store dry over winter for replanting the following spring.
